steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Neurons are nerve cells that transmit electrical impulses. Three types: sensory neurons (carry signals from senses to CNS), relay neurons (connect sensory and motor neurons within the CNS), motor neurons (carry signals from CNS to muscles/glands). | Key Fact: Neuron structure: cell body (contains nucleus), dendrites (receive signals from other neurons), axon (long fibre carrying electrical impulses), myelin sheath (insulates axon, speeds up transmission), terminal buttons (release neurotransmitters at synapses). | Key Fact: Synaptic transmission: when an electrical impulse reaches the end of a neuron, it triggers release of neurotransmitters from vesicles in the terminal buttons.
